formulations.label: Oral suspension
formulations.note: Gastrointestinal absorption is negligible; it acts locally in the mouth and gut.

src.q: Ready mixed oral suspension containing 100,000 units nystatin per ml.
absorption of nystatin from the gastro-intestinal tract is negligible.

formulations.label: Ointment
formulations.note: No UK nystatin-only skin ointment or cream was found (emc and MHRA Products searched); UK topical nystatin exists only in combination products with other actives. Nothing on this page applies to the ointment: no UK source.

bnf.note: BNF/BNFC is only available in the UK; not accessed.

items.t: Oral suspension: prevention and treatment of candidal infections of the mouth, oesophagus and intestinal tract; prophylaxis of oral candidosis in babies born to mothers with vaginal candidosis.

src.q: The prevention and treatment of candidal infections of the oral cavity, oesophagus and intestinal tract.
The suspension provides effective prophylaxis against oral candidosis in those born of mothers with vaginal candidosis.

items.t: Oral preparations should not be used to treat systemic fungal infections.

src.q: Nystatin oral preparations should not be used for treatment of systemic mycoses.

items.t: Adults (denture sores, oral candida): 1 mL dropped into the mouth four times daily, kept in contact with the affected areas as long as possible. Continue for at least 48 hours after symptoms resolve; re-evaluate if not better after 14 days.

src.q: 1 ml of the suspension should be dropped into the mouth four times daily; it should be kept in contact with the affected areas as long as possible.
should be continued for at least 48 hours after symptoms have disappeared.
If signs and symptoms worsen or persist (beyond 14 days of treatment), the patient should be reevaluated, and alternate therapy considered.

items.t: Older people: no specific dose changes.

src.q: No specific dosage recommendations or precautions.

items.t: Infants and children (oral and intestinal thrush): 1 mL into the mouth four times a day. Newborn prophylaxis: 1 mL once daily.

src.q: In intestinal and oral candidosis (thrush) in infants and children, 1 ml should be dropped into the mouth four times a day.
For prophylaxis in the newborn the suggested dose is 1 ml once daily.

items.t: Hypersensitivity to nystatin or any excipient.

src.q: Hypersensitivity to the active substance(s) or to any of the excipients listed in section 6.1.

items.t: Contains sucrose: people with hereditary fructose intolerance, glucose-galactose malabsorption or sucrase-isomaltase insufficiency should not take it. Contains parabens (possible delayed allergy) and a small amount of ethanol.

src.q: Patients with rare hereditary problems of fructose intolerance, glucose-galactose malabsorption or sucrase-isomaltase insufficiency should not take this medicine.
which may cause allergic reactions (possibly delayed).

renal.note: No renal statement in the UK nystatin oral suspension SmPCs; gastrointestinal absorption is negligible.

hepatic.note: No hepatic statement in the UK nystatin oral suspension SmPCs.

items.t: No animal reproduction studies; GI absorption negligible. Prescribe in pregnancy only if the benefit outweighs the potential risk.

src.q: Nystatin should be prescribed during pregnancy only if the potential benefits to be derived outweigh the potential risk to the foetus.

items.t: Not known if excreted in milk; absorption insignificant. Use with caution.

src.q: Although gastrointestinal absorption is insignificant, caution should be exercised when nystatin is prescribed for a nursing woman.

reproductive.note: UK SmPCs state only that effects on reproductive capacity are not known; no specific advice.

items.t: Generally well tolerated. Occasional nausea; large doses may cause diarrhoea, GI upset, nausea and vomiting. (No frequency categories given.)

src.q: Nausea has been reported occasionally during therapy.
Large oral doses of Nystatin have occasionally produced diarrhoea, gastrointestinal distress, nausea and vomiting.

items.t: Hypersensitivity and angioedema (including facial swelling); very rarely Stevens-Johnson syndrome. Stop if irritation or sensitisation develops.

src.q: Hypersensitivity and angioedema, including facial oedema have been reported.
Steven-Johnson Syndrome has been reported very rarely.
If irritation or sensitisation develops, treatment should be discontinued.

items.t: Re-evaluate if symptoms worsen or persist beyond 14 days.

src.q: If signs and symptoms worsen or persist (beyond 14 days of treatment), the patient should be reevaluated, and alternate therapy considered.

items.t: Drop into the mouth; the longer it stays in contact with the affected area before swallowing, the better it works.

src.q: The longer the suspension is kept in contact with the affected area in the mouth, before swallowing, the greater will be its effect.

items.t: Keep using for at least 2 days after symptoms clear; see the doctor if not better after 2 weeks.

src.q: should be continued for at least 48 hours after symptoms have disappeared.
